Highly recommended for anyone craving real Mediterranean food done right!

text.text:
We tried Ay Papa Qué Rico and honestly, it was really good. We ordered the whole charcoal-grilled chicken, congri, yuca, a salad, and a jugo de maracuyá. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. The charbroiled chicken is definitely the star — juicy, well-seasoned, and cooked perfectly over charcoal.
The congri and yuca were solid comfort sides, and the passion fruit juice was refreshing and not overly sweet. For about $65, two of us ate well and still had leftovers to take home — easily enough food for three people.
The vibe is casual and relaxed. It feels like a neighborhood comfort spot with a mix of Cuban, Salvadorian, Guatemalan, and Mexican influences. It’s centered around the charbroiled chicken, but you can tell there’s a little bit of everything on the menu.
If I had to describe it, I’d say it’s comfort food — the kind of place you go when you’re hungry and want something satisfying. It’s definitely an upgrade from places like Pollo Loco. I’d go back.

We started with the drinks, and honestly… they set the tone. The café de olla had that rich, spiced sweetness that feels like a warm hug, while the Thai iced coffee was bold, creamy, and perfectly balanced. The skirt steak chilaquiles were packed with flavor tender steak, rich sauce, and that perfect brunch comfort vibe. And of course, you can’t skip the pancakes… soft, fluffy, and classic in the best way.

The atmosphere is super welcoming, giving you that old-school diner feel in North Hollywood with friendly service that makes you want to stay longer. Whether you’re coming for a casual breakfast, brunch with friends, or just craving something comforting, this spot delivers.

If you’re searching for “best diner in North Hollywood,” “brunch in NoHo,” or “chilaquiles near me,” Hungry Fox definitely deserves a spot on your list. Highly recommend this is one of those places you’ll keep coming back to.

Took my mom here for brunch and overall we had a really nice time. The space is beautiful — very Palm Springs energy with the greenery, open patio, and warm California light. It feels like a little escape in the middle of Studio City. My mom loved it, which automatically makes it a win.

We had a couple glasses of wine and the bill actually came out pretty reasonable, which was a pleasant surprise for a place that looks this polished.

A couple things that were slightly annoying: they make you wait at the bar if your table isn’t ready (which is fine), but then you have to close out your tab at the bar before going to your table. It just feels unnecessary and breaks the flow. Not the end of the world — just mildly irritating.

Food-wise, it’s solid but not mind-blowing. There aren’t a ton of brunch options. The burger was easily the best thing we had — definitely recommend that. The chicken sandwich was… fine. Not bad, just kind of mid.

Parking isn’t the best, and fair warning: if you’re not paying attention, you can easily miss the entrance and end up doing an awkward U-turn near the freeway.

All that said — beautiful vibes, good energy, great for taking your mom or meeting friends for a laid-back brunch. I’d go back, probably for the burger and the atmosphere alone.

editorialSummary.text: Pizza & appetizers in a trendy small-batch craft brewery & taproom open daily until midnight.

text.text:
My love for craft beer brought me here years ago and I still come back often. At one point, they lost their head brewer and we lost a lot of their unique beers but had an array of guest taps. I'm glad that's changed! They're brewing again AND still have guest taps! Deal with the Devil is my favorite IPA here.

Ordering is easy, just go to the bar, place your order (check the paper menus by the register first), open a tab and they'll give you a number to put on your table. Wait for your food to arrive and enjoy! Don't forget the beers!

For food, our go to is always their pizza (check out the cheese pull in my photos) and fougasse. Our kids love the pizza and plain curly fries. Chicken wings and their Caesar salad is good too!

We miss the panna cotta they used to have. They were delicious! The cookies are a good substitute for that sweet craving after a meal.

Parking can be difficult and stressful at times to find a spot. You'll have to drive around to find one. They have parking in front of the brewery, but it's VERY limited. We Uber with friends and family sometimes to avoid the stress of finding parking.

Staff is always kind and always there to make suggestions on the beers they serve.

Don't forget to take a photo in their photo booth before you leave! For $7, you'll be able to take 3 photos and the machine will print two copies for you. Awesome souvenir that you and your partner will be able to take one home!

Parking can be difficult and stressful at times to find a spot. You'll have to drive around to find one. They have parking in front of the brewery, but it's VERY limited. We Uber with friends and family sometimes to avoid the stress of finding parking.

Staff is always kind and always there to make suggestions on the beers they serve.

There’s really nothing much to say except…..WHERE IS IT!?
My brother, his lady and myself were really excited to check out the food here, especially me because I’d never had African food before. When we arrived at the location we had to circle the block 3 times just to be sure we had the correct address, which we did. The “location” sits on the corner of an industrial/isolated block, it was very confusing before nothing about the exterior of the structure resembled a restaurant. No aroma of goat, curry, beef or chicken in the air, no cars parked directly in front of the establishment, no foot traffic, no signs up with the name of the restaurant on it. Nothing. So many red flags. We asked a man who was loading the back of his truck in the driveway nearby about the place (because it appeared to be closed) and he assured us that it was open and to follow the sign to Suite #8. Now once we stepped inside of the “place” it was completely empty (inside resembled a a touch swap meet familiarity, but eery). The man told us suite #8 but the sign said, “The Peppered Goat” #12….so we walked around and looked for it. Thinking about now gives me the creeps because it was so quiet with an occasional soft sound here and there but nothing of a restaurant or food establishment, and STILL no smell or inclination of food being cooked. We had to walk down, around and through these very narrow corridors that were full of equipment of some sort, we called out for people and knocked on other suite doors but we got nothing. No response from anyone. When came out we saw the same man still outside digging around the back of his truck and we told him no one was in there and there definitely weren’t any restaurants in there (it literally would have been impossible to have one in there - where? how?). The man said,”Ohhh, I guess they’re shutdown now!” and laughed. As soon as we pulled off we all got freaked out. It literally felt like a scene in a horror movie & I love horror but it felt like we were the 3 black people that gets killed in the very beginning of movie 🤭
I definitely didn’t mean to turn this review into a horror story but it’s the truth. The moral to the story is DON’T GO!

I originally came here just for a smoothie and coffee, but I didn’t try the food at first. Later, I met one of the employees, and he told me that I really needed to try something from their menu. So when I came back the second time, even though I didn’t have much time, I decided to order a sandwich.

Honestly, it was very good. I always write only honest reviews, and I never leave reviews for money because my Google account and reputation are important to me. The coffee was excellent, with nicely roasted beans. The sandwich was perfectly toasted, fresh, and tasty. The bread was fresh, the turkey was very good, and their special chef’s sauce made it even better. The greens were fresh and nicely dressed — I’m not exactly sure what they used, but it tasted great.

They also have a big menu, and I definitely want to come back and try more. One more thing I really appreciated: I came almost at closing time and needed to use the restroom. It was for employees only, but after I kindly asked, they helped me and allowed me to use it. When I passed by the kitchen, I noticed how clean everything was, and that made me trust the place even more.

Overall, great food, great coffee, clean kitchen, and kind staff. I will definitely stop by from time to time.

The food is delicious, the people are kind and sweet. Yesterday was my first day here and I had the spicy chicken sandwich which was phenomenal. Came back today for the breakfast burrito with organic chicken sausage added inside, I didn’t know I could like chicken sausage so much 😅 the food is delicious, but it’s not the filling yourself up for the sake of it kind of delicious. It’s the kind of where your body actually feels like what you eat is good for you. I almost never entered this area because the parking area looked intimidating, but I realize that it does flare up, but it stays relatively open after those bad moments.

There was a gentleman helping me yesterday. I don’t know if he was the owner, but he was also very kind, today there was a Sweet cashier I think by the name of Ately but I’ve probably got that name wrong. 😅 they are both very welcoming, it’s refreshing to enter an establishment and almost feel as though they’re happy to see you. Not get the sensation that the people are just clocking in and they want you to leave immediately after your purchase. The food does take a few minutes to prepare, and evidently they bake all of their goods,

The music is a little old school, but I like it. There isn’t a lot of seats not exactly the best place possibly for a big group, but unlike other establishment that is revolving, people are coming and going consistently. That’s usually a good sign. They don’t stay open past 5 PM so they don’t really have a dinner menu but it seems like it’s more of a breakfast to lunch kind of thing.

It’s impossible for me to sit here and tell you how good the food tastes in my mouth so I’m not even gonna bother. I will tell you that it’s absolutely worth trying at least once. That the smoothie is appeared to be almost exclusively, fresh fruit, coffee is not bad at all. And conveniently they give you your coffee in it to go cup so you could just dip whenever you want.

I see myself coming here very often now. I’ve been pretty bored with a lot of the food selection in my area. I’ve been honestly looking for a place like this and I’m happy I found one.

They have desserts and pastries,  but honestly aside from the delicious food, the thing that’s most significant to me and my favorite part is this. At least, with the current staff, it’s warm and welcoming. Sitting down to eat in this restaurant doesn’t feel like any other fast food joint or the fake pleasant trees of overwork waiters in other places. It’s a nice and comfortable atmosphere. As a guy who lives alone and spent most of his time either working or alone. It’s hard to ignore how cozy the feel is at this place. I hope that stays the same.

Highly recommend, and I would like to be more of a regular there personally…

I’m the person who usually walks into businesses hired to restore them. It’s rare these days I write a review. This is written not just due to a quick impression by one visit, or how invested I am as a consumer based on one meal or one employee who was friendly - this is a 360 perspective on a business doing it right.

When I pause to look and recognize somewhere who “gets it” organically, it means something. This is long but, they’ve earned it.

Context - I just moved back to Los Angeles from Seattle. I’ve never lived North of the 101, I have no local haunts up here, and I’m still getting settled. Finding a new role, not yet in a groove and all I knew was that I missed good food. One morning I searched for an almond croissant and landed on Victory Cafe.

I typed a note on my delivery receipt warning them in jest and CA humor I’d be ordering batches of five croissants at a time because I was in love with their menu. And I meant it. I’m a creature of habit - Salads for dinner, sandwiches, quesadillas, kids’ scrambles with fruit and sides of bacon — all with four to six croissants added every time.

By week two, order three or four, my phone rings after I place an order. It’s the owner, Efren, talking to me like I’ve been a client for years. He tells me I’m a VIP to him and his team. They know my orders. That day they were out of my almond croissants, and he asked if I’d mind if he stayed late, made a batch himself, and personally dropped them off on his way home at 7 pm. He threw in some other pastries and muffins to try - c’mon - has that ever happened to you?!

He’s not the pastry chef. This was a homemade croissant — not a waffle. He didn’t even ask how far away I was. And he did exactly what he said he would. He told me he remembered my receipt note about just moving back to LA, and he wanted to make sure I was taken care of by his team.

I just placed another order and my phone rang again. I braced for a substitution call — fair enough, it’s 4 p.m. and I ordered eight pastries. But it was Efren, just saying hi. Checking on me. “We have everything for you today, but I wanted to say hello and see how you were.”

The food is outstanding. I get enough to last me two to three days for under $50 and it’s better than anything else I’ve found. It’s fresh, healthy and it’s home cooked meals. They cater to vegans if that’s your preference. But where else are you treated like this without even walking in — just ordering through Grubhub? Imagine when I dine in! I’m treated like family and I am confident I’ve moved to the right place if I’ve landed near a restaurant with people who are this wonderful.

I’ll be loyal to Victory Cafe for life. And I’ll drive to them no matter where I end up getting an apartment down the line. It’s a simple but rare thing: quality, consistency, genuine kindness, and a customer relationship that’s actually substantive. I’d trust Efren with more than an order, and his team reflects training that is preparing them for careers and life long values — at his organization and beyond. Keep an eye on Victory Cafe. It takes more than an owner to create this kind of magic. Well done, team.

Stopped at Victory Caffe on our drive back to SF from LA after seeing the great reviews, and it definitely lived up to them. It’s a small family-run spot with a really welcoming atmosphere.

The owner, Efrien (hope I got the name right), was incredibly kind and patient. While we were there, another customer was upset about a delayed online order, but he handled the situation calmly and respectfully the whole time. That alone left a great impression on us.

We ordered the spicy chicken sandwich, an egg sandwich, and cappuccinos. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and reasonably priced for the portion sizes. The coffee was especially good.

They also offer many vegetarian and healthy options. Definitely worth a stop if you’re passing through the area!

I tried their kebab, and honestly the beef had an unusually salty taste — I was thirsty the whole day afterwards. The chicken kebab was seasoned more moderately. The salad was standard, nothing special. The rice was tasty but not fully steamed through. Overall, I can’t say the other dishes really impressed me. Maybe some people enjoy this style, but the marinade had a specific aftertaste that I personally didn’t like, and it made me drink water all day.

The sauce for the kebab was just a simple mix of ketchup, mayo, and some herbs. The hummus was fresh and actually very good. The portion was big, and the dishes looked nice visually. There’s parking available, around ten tables inside — a decent place to stop by for a quick meal. I might come back someday to try something else. They also offer larger platters for groups, which can be convenient if you’re coming with friends or family. The presentation looks nice, and the portions are generous, so it can work well for sharing.

I come to Mediterranean Fresh Grill often, but unfortunately my experience with phone orders has been disappointing more than once.

At least twice, I’ve called to place an order and was put on hold, only for nobody to come back and take my order. Most recently, I called ahead and was told my food would be ready in 20 minutes. Because I have a very busy schedule, I rely on ordering ahead to save time.

When I arrived 20 minutes later, they told me they didn’t have my order and even asked if I had called the right location. The employee went to the back, came back, and proceeded to charge me. At that point, I assumed my food was about to come out. When I asked how much longer it would take, I was told another 15–20 minutes.

That means my order would have taken nearly an hour from the time I first called. The restaurant wasn’t busy, yet no one apologized or seemed concerned about the inconvenience. The response was simply that they didn’t have my order.

I’ve been a regular customer for a long time, but it feels like customer service is no longer a priority. It’s disappointing because the food is good, but there are plenty of other places that value their customers’ time and business.
